object_description: upper body carried on freely placed massive piers over a landscaped ground-level walking space
design_condition: the piers of the structure are freely placed at ground level following a pavilion logic while the upper body adopts the language and orientation of the neighbouring polytechnic complex, connecting user flows at both levels

positive: The jury is interested by the desire to form a link between the two built fabrics
The intention is verified in the implementation of the built masses by a fairly subtle strategy
The piers are located freely at ground level following a characteristic pavilion logic
The upper body carried by these piles adopts the language of the polytechnic complex
The device effectively connects user flows at ground level and via the gateway
The main axis is recognised as a vital connection and finds its missing western gateway
The approach jointly constructs interior and exterior spaces until the distinction disappears
The building constructs the site at the same time as the site gives form to the architecture
The jury welcomes this approach and notes its relevance to the question posed
The conceptual principle of the ground floor as architectural exterior or landscaped interior is recognised
The exterior arrangements could be improved
negative: The entrance from the avenue is only a delivery access alongside technical premises
The singular, spectacular result with expressionist emphasis raises questions of decor and kitsch
No good constructive reasons support the formal proposal
The thick slab device amplifies rather than resolves the structural issues
The formal gratuity presents additional cost and complications
The spectacular formalisation may break abruptly with the calm continuity of the existing path
The banal and mechanical typology on the floors lacks the expected spatial richness
The attention to public space would have benefited from resonance in the study and living space
The significant floor depth poses serious questions of natural lighting
A significant part of the programme is not covered, a deficit of 883 square metres
The research building has no reception space and the cafeteria has no toilets
Programmatic inconsistencies and unsatisfactory flow management from long corridors
Service premises risk being used as horizontal distribution
The construction does not fit the sustainability objectives in terms of grey energy
The ground floor recovery slab lies outside the thermal envelope, risking expansion and cracking
It has abundant excess thickness, execution complications and thermal bridges
The absence of glazing with openings is regretted
Significant cuts in the existing vegetation are criticised
The exterior arrangements are expensive and the cost of the work is above average
